web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: What earnings recovery and cash-flow profile does NKE price in at $32.92, and how does that compare with athletic peers?

epigraph.quote: A low trailing multiple built on one-time tariff recoveries can hide an expensive forward earnings trough.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $32.92 (TradingView feed $32.94), NIKE, Inc. carries a market capitalization of $48.90 billion across roughly 1.485 billion diluted shares [23, 38, 43]. Public screeners often show only the 1.20 billion Class B shares. Yet Swoosh, LLC and insiders hold another 281 million convertible Class A shares [38, 43]. As of August 31, 2026, funded debt was $7,893 million and operating lease liabilities stood at $3,179 million [37]. Subtracting $8,368 million in cash and short-term investments yields $2,704 million in lease-adjusted net debt [37]. That lifts NIKE's lease-adjusted Enterprise Value to $51.60 billion [43].

Headline trailing multiples look cheap at first glance. Finviz shows a trailing P/E of 15.78x on $2.09 trailing EPS and an EV/Sales ratio of 1.12x [43]. However, FY2026 net income ($3,108 million) leaned on a $986 million Q4 IEEPA tariff recovery worth ~$0.53 per share after tax [1, 2]. Stripping out that windfall puts underlying FY2026 earnings near $1.55 per share.

Management's November 17, 2026 Investor Day (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1) reset FY2027 far lower [32]. Guidance calls for a high-single-digit revenue drop and an adjusted operating margin near 6% (down from 8.2% in FY2026) [32]. Adjusted EPS is guided to $1.15–$1.35, excluding ~$0.15 per share in Pace restructuring costs [32]. At $32.92, NKE trades at 26.3x the $1.25 FY2027 adjusted EPS midpoint and 29.9x GAAP midpoint earnings [32].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: What Cash-Flow Recovery Is Already Priced In?

web_blocks.html: A reverse discounted cash flow model shows what future cash flows justify today's $51.60 billion Enterprise Value. We apply a 9.0% weighted average cost of capital (WACC) and a 2.5% terminal growth rate [38]. Our discount rate reflects the 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield and higher credit spreads after 2025 rating downgrades [38]. In Q1 FY2027, free cash flow turned negative at -$64 million [37]. With ~$1.3 billion in Pace restructuring charges ahead, FY2027 unlevered free cash flow will likely compress toward $1.0–$1.4 billion [32].

Justifying a $51.60 billion Enterprise Value at a 9.0% discount rate requires a steep rebound. NIKE must lift annual revenue back toward $48–$50 billion by FY2031. Operating margins must also recover from ~6% to at least 10.5%–11.5%. That path requires $3.6–$4.0 billion in normalized annual free cash flow by FY2029–FY2030. Management targets 12%–14% operating margins by FY2031, leaving thin margin for execution slips [32].

web_blocks.caption: NIKE, Inc. Reverse DCF & Implied Expectations Matrix at $32.92 (WACC 9.0%, Terminal Growth 2.5%)
web_blocks.takeaway: At $32.92, the market already prices in a smooth recovery from ~6% FY2027 margins toward 10.5%–11.0% by FY2031; if China losses and $15.5B endorsement rigidity cap margins near 8.5%, intrinsic value drops toward $23.50 [32, 37].

web_blocks.the_number: $32.20 per share (12-month Base Case fair value, -2.2% vs. $32.92 CMP).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We anchor 12-month fair value to an explicit FY2028E EBIT-to-EPS bridge rather than depressed FY2027 trough EPS ($1.25 midpoint). We cross-check that multiple against our lease-adjusted Reverse DCF base path.
web_blocks.the_inputs: FY2027E revenue falls 8% to ~$42.7B at ~6.0% adjusted operating margin ($2.56B EBIT, $1.25 adj. EPS). In FY2028E, revenue stabilizes near $43.3B (+1.5%) and operating margin edges up 100 bps to 7.0% ($3.03B EBIT). Adding ~$45M net interest/other yields $3.08B pre-tax income; a 20.3% tax rate leaves $2.45B net income, or $1.65 EPS across 1.485B shares (+32% recovery ahead of Pace's FY29–FY30 ramp and Finviz's +3.85% consensus). At 19.5x, fair value is $32.18 (~$32.20).
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $23.50 (18.0x $1.30 FY28E EPS if China stays down 15%–20% and margin stalls near 5.5%) to Bull $43.00 (22.0x $1.95 FY28E EPS if Pace pulls savings ahead of FY29).
web_blocks.if_off: Even our Base Case embeds a constructive +32% FY2028 EPS rebound and still sits below $32.92. If Pace stalls or Q2 earnings on December 17 miss $0.38, shares could fall toward $23.50.

web_blocks.title: Historical Valuation Bands & Dividend Coverage Stress

web_blocks.html: Over the past five years, NKE dropped 81% from its pandemic peak [43]. Investors once paid 30x–35x earnings for 15% operating margins and 25%+ ROIC. Today's 4.98% trailing dividend yield ($1.64 TTM; $1.66 estimated) offers optical income support [43]. Yet Finviz's 77.7% trailing payout ratio hides real strain [43]. Against FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance ($1.15–$1.35), the ~$1.66 dividend (~$2.46 billion cash outlay) represents a 133% payout ratio [32]. NIKE must draw down cash reserves until margins recover [32, 36].

Pairing that snapshot with SEC filings for On Holding (Q3 2026 Form 6-K) and annual reports for adidas and ANTA reveals a sharp margin gap [14, 17, 39, 40].

book_paragraphs: At the November 20, 2026 closing price of $32.92, NIKE, Inc. carries a market capitalization of $48.90 billion across roughly 1.485 billion diluted shares. Retail screeners often display only the 1.20 billion public Class B shares, overlooking 281 million Class A shares held mainly by Swoosh, LLC. Adding $7.89 billion of funded debt and $3.18 billion of operating lease liabilities, less $8.37 billion in cash, puts lease-adjusted net debt at $2.70 billion and Enterprise Value at $51.60 billion.

Trailing multiples look cheap at 15.78x earnings and 1.12x sales, yet those figures mislead. FY2026 net income leaned on a $986 million Q4 IEEPA tariff recovery worth roughly $0.53 per share after tax. Without that windfall, underlying FY2026 earnings sit closer to $1.55 per share. More critically, the November 17 Investor Day cut FY2027 revenue to a high-single-digit decline, compressed adjusted operating margins to ~6%, and guided adjusted EPS to $1.15–$1.35. At $32.92, investors pay 26.3x the $1.25 FY2027 adjusted midpoint for a shrinking business.

Our reverse DCF model tests what $32.92 already assumes. Using a 9.0% cost of capital and 2.5% terminal growth, a $51.60 billion Enterprise Value requires normalized free cash flow to rebuild toward $3.6–$3.8 billion annually by FY2029–FY2030. That demands operating margins expanding back to 10.5%–11.0% on $48–$50 billion of sales. Since Pace's $2.5 billion cost savings do not ramp until FY2029 and FY2030, today's price gives management credit years in advance.

Anchoring 12-month fair value to an explicit FY2028 EBIT-to-EPS bridge confirms the lack of upside buffer. If revenue stabilizes near $43.3 billion in FY2028 (+1.5%) and operating margin expands 100 bps from ~6% to 7.0% ($3.03B EBIT), adding ~$45M net non-operating income yields $3.08B pre-tax income and $2.45B net income ($1.65 EPS at a 20.3% tax rate). Even that constructive +32% earnings recovery ahead of Pace's FY29 ramp and Finviz's +3.85% consensus yields just $32.20 at 19.5x—below today's close.

Dividend math adds further strain. While the trailing $1.64 payout shows a 4.98% yield, ~$2.4 billion in annual dividends now exceed FY2026 free cash flow ($2.18 billion) and guided FY2027 earnings. Share buybacks have stalled, and cash fell $659 million in Q1 FY2027 alone despite collecting $684 million in tariff cash. Rigid $15.5 billion athlete endorsement guarantees and $1.3 billion in Pace restructuring costs limit how quickly cash burn can reverse.

Peer multiples highlight the valuation gap. Deckers Outdoor trades at 9.60x forward P/E with a 23.47% operating margin and 44.27% ROE, while On Holding grew Q3 revenue +17.2% at a 66.9% ex-tariff gross margin. Meanwhile, adidas is reclaiming European and football mindshare, and ANTA Sports dominates domestic tiers in China. Even Deckers sits in Stage 4 as HOKA slows to +6.8%, making NKE's 26.3x FY2027E multiple tough to justify.

Ultimately, valuation is a function of capital efficiency and time. At 13% trailing ROIC, NIKE still clears its 9% cost of capital, yet ROIC has fallen far from its 25%–30% peak. Until FY2029 Pace savings begin lifting operating margins above 10% and free cash flow comfortably covers the $2.4 billion annual dividend, paying 26.3x trough earnings offers poor compensation for multi-year execution risk.

Examining Reverse DCF expectations side by side with direct specialty competitors highlights why valuation alone cannot rescue a broken chart. At $32.92, NIKE carries a $51.60 billion lease-adjusted enterprise value that demands operating margin recovery toward roughly 8.5 percent and $3.6 billion to $3.8 billion in normalized free cash flow under a 9.0 percent cost of capital. Yet first-quarter cash generation turned negative at -$64 million even after collecting the bulk of the remaining $684 million IEEPA tariff receivable.

Relative peer multiples sharpen this valuation ceiling further. Deckers Outdoor trades near 9.60 times forward earnings with a 23.47 percent operating margin and double-digit returns on invested capital, while On Holding continues capturing running specialty shelf space above a 66 percent ex-tariff gross margin. Until NIKE demonstrates clear fiscal 2028 operating leverage above the 7.0 percent milestone embedded in our $32.20 Base Case bridge, owning NKE above $30 offers negligible risk-adjusted compensation.
